title: Selection sort
summary: Find the smallest value that is left, and swap it into the next place.

checkpoints.text: Looking for the smallest value from cell 0 onwards. 10 is smaller than 29, so `minIndex` now marks cell 1.
The scan found 5 at the end, the smallest of all. One swap puts it in cell 0, its final place.
Second round: the smallest of what is left is 10, which is already in cell 1, so it is swapped with itself. Cells 0 and 1 are done.
5 10 13 14 29 37. Selection sort always makes about n²/2 comparisons, sorted input or not, so it is Θ(n²). But it makes at most n - 1 swaps, fewer than bubble sort.
